# FG-01-I — Discover and Bind Host
<!-- regression-guard: not-applicable -->

## What & Why

Bind Piece 01 to the actual Skills Workbench Project, extract the canonical Failure Gate v4 obligations, and establish factual installation boundaries before later pieces. This is a source/discovery and tracked-document task only, not a runtime installation. Narrow protection: preserve source/evidence provenance, unknown states, existing coverage, and independent review; do not fabricate runtime results.

## Binding, owner, inputs, and outputs

Owner: implementation agent; confirm actual host roles rather than inventing a person or service. Target is the current Project task-board context and repository root observed as `/home/runner/workspace` (Skills Workbench). Reconfirm Project and root before substantive reads or target writes; stop on mismatch. Platform task refs are not Failure Gate local IDs.

Inputs: the complete tracked 18-piece specification `docs/validation/failure-gate-v4-task-series.md`, the Piece 01 supplement, current canonical `.agents` source closure, actual Project instructions/configuration, existing policy/capability/evidence/task records, and only genuinely permitted read-only access routes. Archived #66/#67 are stale historical drafts, not dependencies, authority, or reusable tasks.

Deliver tracked Piece 01 records in the established `docs/validation/` layout: discovery report, immutable canonical source manifest, full obligation/acceptance allocation, capability manifest, initial evidence-index reconciliation, prior-policy/caller inventory, installation-scope proposal, and installer handoff. Reuse the existing descriptive capability locator and evidence index; do not create a competing authority or mutate live stores.

## Done looks like

- Project identity, repository root, current source/config snapshot, allowed stage, report destinations, actual roles and task/plan bindings are evidenced; unresolved identity blocks target work.
- The full canonical Failure Gate closure and applicable Router closure are pinned to immutable paths/revisions/digests; reference cycles are visited once per pinned revision; current source drift is reconciled, not silently normalized.
- A clause-by-clause ledger covers every applicable obligation and acceptance case assigned across Pieces 01–18, including justified multi-piece acceptance; source meaning and evidence rules are not weakened.
- Actual host language/runtime, validation commands/callers, governance and coverage, task/plan formats, persistence, approval source, completion writer, locks, supervision/providers, recovery, budgets and optional history/catalog are inventoried from original sources/read-only records.
- Capability/evidence records use actual safe locations and procedures, explicit present/missing/unavailable states, named roles and next actions. Canonical source availability, Project implementation/readiness, and platform task lifecycle remain separate claims.
- The installation proposal distinguishes source staging from runtime permissions, records actual dependencies and finite authority where verified, and leaves every unresolved capability blocked/unknown rather than ready.
- The installer handoff carries exact source/report/evidence bindings to the dependent verifier without claiming contract installation, host acceptance, ordinary activation, or cutover.

## Out of scope

- Runtime enforcement, policy/approval/tier change, store initialization or mutation, coordinator/CLI invocation, imports, syntax checks, tests, typechecks, builds, startup, services/workflows, signals, recovery, caller wiring, reclaim, cutover, remote CI, merge, deploy, or Piece 02–18 task cards.
- Editing canonical skill definitions or using `.local` mirrors/archives as normative sources.
- Reopening or rewriting archived #66/#67.

## Shared authorization and validation contract

At execution, determine governing policy as ACTIVE, INACTIVE, or UNKNOWN from actual evidence. ACTIVE uses its existing checked route; INACTIVE uses independently verified existing host policy and equivalent finite supervision; UNKNOWN blocks dependent execution. Invalid explicit checked requests never fall back. Bootstrap, ordinary activation, diagnostic, recovery, reclaim, and cutover are separate authority domains. No task-board status or task approval is a local Failure Gate approval.

Resolve actual approved phase/queue/step/startup/test/hook/teardown/cancellation/termination/capture/parent/session/attempt/resource limits from an authentic source. Do not invent defaults or reuse the already-consumed one-shot health-only bootstrap. Require independent whole-tree supervision, bounded reads/capture, original accounting, cleanup reserve, and a pinned transitive graph before dispatch. Run only one selected approved tier or named bounded capability; no sweep, arbitrary passthrough, retry, or budget reset. This Piece 01 task launches none of them.

A verifier may repair only the declared documentary scope. Repair does not authorize policy approval, budget increase, recovery, disruption, activation, cutover, CI, merge, or deployment. Any such need is a separate exact blocker/proposal.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Reconfirm the actual Project/task-board context and root before substantive work. Record the verified scope and actual owner roles; stop target-dependent work if they differ from the observed Skills Workbench workspace.
2. Read only canonical sources under `.agents/skills/failure-gate-v4/` and `.agents/skills/skill-application-router/`, including all applicable transitive implementation/acceptance resources and tests. Pin immutable digests and record missing/unavailable resources. Never use runtime mirrors, attached copies, or prior summaries as canonical definitions.
3. Re-read the planning digest table. Ten listed Failure Gate entry digests matched at planning time. Three listed Router digests differed; current values observed were: Router `SKILL.md` `49e3db86b0f5b8c7efba871d7404c40336cb3caf544427a429065b1088f6586f`, `references/installation-verification-plan.md` `99bc98079967ed47f8f524c187b9823fc99dddca55d4b61a9220dcbb5b3f8cb9`, and `references/handoff-binding-and-recovery.md` `7e95d74645e0c1184b2ae24488ffd5936237fb6fc1d9596734a3e57bb1fe0ff5`. Preserve both baselines, explain/reconcile all differences, and pin current delivery-reconciliation and task-handoff-acceptance references too.
4. Extract every applicable canonical obligation and acceptance case into a stable ledger; assign it to the exact Piece 01–18 owner from the attached spec, including evidence, applicability, owner, dependency and pass/fail rule. Shared acceptance has a reasoned multi-piece allocation. Missing source or ambiguous allocation is blocked, not guessed.
5. Verify current host facts from original records. Existing docs describe ordinary governance as STAGED, the health-only bootstrap as consumed, API generation as denied, live writer participation as unverified, and reclaim as blocked; independently recheck these without treating descriptive manifests as authority. Do not initialize a missing store or invoke any discovered command.
6. Preserve existing callers, commands, reports, coverage, configuration and history. Separate code/source placement from registered routes, approved authority, operational proof and platform task state. Document unknown external/transitive callers and optional catalog/history absence.
7. Publish the specified discovery evidence, reconcile existing capability/evidence locators in place only within permitted document scope, and provide an installation proposal and handoff with named owners, concrete next actions, stage gates and evidence destinations.
8. Do not create/surface Pieces 02–18 or approve/activate any task. No Failure Gate local ID is allocated here. Do not execute runtime checks or alter any authority, store, process, remote workflow, or deployment.

## Steps

1. Confirm Project identity, repository root, governing stage, host roles, and exact permitted read/write scope before substantive inspection; stop on mismatch or missing authority.
2. Pin the canonical Failure Gate and Router closures, compare the attached planning hashes with current sources, and retain all drift and missing-resource evidence.
3. Inventory actual host routes and records for validation, callers, governance, task/plan data, persistence, decisions, completion, locks, supervision, recovery, budgets, and coverage without executing discovered commands or initializing stores.
4. Build the complete 18-piece requirement/acceptance ledger, capability/evidence map, prior-policy/caller inventory, source/runtime stage boundaries, and owner/action mapping for each gap.
5. Publish and reconcile the Piece 01 report, manifest, ledger, existing descriptive locators, proposal, and installer handoff; preserve evidence lineage and unknown states.
6. Record actual prerequisites, finite limits/consumption only when authoritatively known, exclusions, and the exact next scoped proposal. Leave all unapproved runtime operations blocked.

## Evidence and blocked handling

Link each claim to the original source path/section, actual record, revision/digest and observation time; label it documented, implemented, registered, deployed, or independently verified. Retain the source manifest, all ledger rows, capability/evidence references, host inventory, baseline drift, and raw permitted observations. Distinguish fixture result from host acceptance and source parity from runtime readiness. Never include secrets or fabricate approvals/tests/results.

If Project identity, canonical source, actual approval/budget/supervision, safe read route, evidence store, role, or report write permission is missing, record the exact missing item, responsible role and next action; continue only independent permitted discovery. Do not use an expired/consumed grant. Any required test, CLI/store/service/signal/recovery/cutover action is blocked outside this scope.

## Pre-existing failures to ignore

None are authorized by this plan. Preserve existing observed failures and incomplete history as owned/unresolved evidence; do not infer pre-existing provenance or invent a catalog ignore.

## Validation

Route: bounded canonical-source and host-record readback plus document/evidence-link consistency only, if actually permitted. **readback-only / execution not authorized** for tests, scripts, CLI, imports, builds, store initialization, services, workflows, signals or remote checks. No tier, authorization, budget, supervisor or diagnostic capability is inferred. Record actual bindings and remaining consumption if a valid route is discovered; otherwise state blocked and name its owner. Do not claim a validation PASS.

sourceClauses.text: ### FG-04-I — Stage workload gate and whole-tree supervision
**Input/dependency:** FG-03-V; verified candidate host containment/supervision boundary.
**Implement:**
- Integrate the real external supervisor/job provider, independent of the supervised event loop. Do not substitute a mock supervisor or same-process timer.
- Journal the private workload-gate identity and require independent registration acknowledgement before user dispatch; failed registration denies work.
- Bind original monotonic remaining deadlines and phase/attempt lineage; retain reserved cancellation, termination, verification, and evidence time.
- Track exact owned process/job incarnations and children, including permitted remote targets; handle owner stall/death, original-group timeout, watchdog loss, and newly observed descendants.
- Bound pre-dispatch reads and combined stdout/stderr collection during streaming/spooling. Validate typed stop/report/storage acknowledgements.

- Preserve exclusion and original partial evidence on unknown termination, capture overflow, or post-spawn journal failure; cleanup already owned work within its grant without depending on a healthy journal.
- Keep source staging separate from live listener cleanup/reclaim.
**Acceptance:** Source is ready for a safely admitted first proof. Missing real independent containment blocks that proof; it does not justify an uncontained hang experiment.

sourceClauses.text: ### FG-18-V — Independently verify the complete installed contract and repair gaps now

Perform fresh full canonical-to-host verification of every applicable ledger item, not a collection of installer summaries. Revalidate all earlier evidence against current affected inputs, wiring, approved definitions, environment, and this verifier's complete payload.

This verifier explicitly includes safe scoped repairs for omissions in any preceding implementation piece. List gaps first, trace each to its owning requirement/piece, patch the missing/wrong implementation within approved installation scope, renew changed enforcement approval where required, and rerun affected checks under real authority and retained budgets. Perform an independent post-repair readback. Do not recurse into more verifier tasks or fix unrelated product defects.
Recheck that:
- Canonical instructions/references are available and source parity is accurately reported.

- No project code/CLI depends on platform-managed completion; platform task status remains a separate claim.
- All failed/blocked/not-run checks, unresolved repairs, unsafe legacy risks, missing providers, and retained exclusions remain visible.

**Not approved, not registered, not launched.**
